models.purpose: Model the viral spread dynamics of Wordle score-sharing behavior using four compartments (Potential, Crowd, Quitted, Loyal) analogous to epidemiological SIR, fitted with genetic algorithm + Nelder-Mead, with Bootstrap prediction intervals.
models.summary: A 4-compartment ODE system (PCQL) extending SIR by splitting Recovered into Quitted and Loyal, capturing the persistence of habitual players. Parameters alpha (participation), beta (boredom), gamma (conversion), delta (loyal boredom). Fitted via genetic algorithm for initial solution then Nelder-Mead for MSE minimization. Bootstrap (1000 samples) provides 95% prediction intervals. Predicts March 1 2023 report count in [11173, 17069].

Habitual TPers who persist

governing_equations.label: PCQL-1
governing_equations.purpose: Potential population depletion through contact with active TPers.

governing_equations.label: PCQL-2
governing_equations.source_expression: dC(t)/dt = alpha * P(t) * (C(t) + L(t)) / N - beta * C(t) - gamma * C(t)
governing_equations.purpose: Crowd dynamics: inflow from Potential minus outflow to Quitted and Loyal.

governing_equations.label: PCQL-3
governing_equations.purpose: Quitted population accumulation from bored crowd members.

governing_equations.label: PCQL-4
governing_equations.purpose: Loyal player dynamics: conversion from crowd minus loyal attrition.

equation_status.reason: All four PCQL ODE equations transcribed from p.12.

objectives: Model the spread dynamics of Wordle score-sharing behavior and predict future report counts.
constraints: Total population N = P(0) + C(0) + Q(0) + L(0) is conserved.

details: P(0) = N, C(0) = initial TPers, Q(0) = 0, L(0) = 0.
Long-term behavior is asymptotic decay, not analyzed as equilibrium.

parameter_estimation.method: Genetic algorithm for initial solution; Nelder-Mead for MSE minimization. Fitted alpha=1.77e-01, beta=1.77e-02, gamma=1.04e-03, delta=1.14e-03.

steps: Solve ODE numerically for given parameters.
Compute MSE between numerical solution and observed report counts.
Genetic algorithm global search for parameter initialization.
Nelder-Mead local optimization from GA initial point.
Bootstrap 1000 resamples with Nelder-Mead for prediction intervals.

assumptions: Consistency of Behavior: TPers do TP every day, non-TPers never do.
Viral Marketing: conversion probability proportional to contact with active TPers.
Potential Customers: only a subset of non-TPers can become TPers.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Parameters identified via GA + Nelder-Mead; fitted values reported. Bootstrap provides uncertainty bounds.

validation_refs: R-squared not reported for ODE fit; visual fit shown in Figure 4. Bootstrap 95% CI [11173, 17069] for March 1 2023.
models.computational_cost: GA initial search + 1000 Bootstrap Nelder-Mead fits.
strengths: Mechanistic interpretation of viral spread with loyal-player extension.
missing_details: ODE solver details (step size, method) not specified.

models.section: 5 Is Word Itself affect Hard Mode Ratio
models.purpose: Test whether word attributes (regularity) explain the Hard Mode report percentage.
models.summary: Simple linear regression of Hard Mode percentage on weighted/unweighted regularity. R-squared = 0.022 (weighted) and 0.013 (unweighted), both negligible. Conclusion: word attributes do not meaningfully affect Hard Mode ratio; the observed correlation is a temporal confound.

governing_equations.purpose: Linear regression of Hard Mode percentage on weighted regularity.

constraints: Standard assumptions of the method apply.

models.purpose: Predict the distribution of Wordle try-counts for a given puzzle word based on word features.
models.summary: KNN regression (K=15) using word frequency, number of repeated letters, weighted purity, weighted regularity, and max repetitions as features. Predicts 7-bin distribution (1-try through X). Cross-validated MSE = 12.35. Applied to predict EERIE distribution: (0.20, 4.87, 23.55, 35.36, 23.75, 9.94, 2.33). Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals about 5% above/below predicted values.

governing_equations.label: KNN-reg
governing_equations.purpose: KNN regression: average of K nearest neighbors' response vectors.

objectives: Predict 7-bin try distribution for any puzzle word.
constraints: Predicted distribution sums to 100% by construction.

parameter_estimation.method: 10-fold cross-validation for K selection. Best K=15, MSE=12.35.

steps: Compute Euclidean distance between test word and all training words.

assumptions: Words with similar features have similar try distributions.
Euclidean distance in standardized feature space is meaningful.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: K selected by CV. Sum-to-100% guaranteed by averaging.

validation_refs: Figure 10 cross-validation results; Figure 11 Bootstrap CI for EERIE.
models.computational_cost: Low for K=15; Bootstrap adds 1000 refits.
limitations: Does not model temporal player-structure changes.
missing_details: Distance metric details (weighted vs unweighted Euclidean).

models.purpose: Classify puzzle words into difficulty categories (easy/normal/hard) based on word features.
models.summary: KNN classifier (K=8) using number of repeated letters, weighted purity, and weighted regularity. Three difficulty levels based on median try count (3=easy, 4=normal, 5-6=hard). Cross-validated accuracy 75.28%, confidence interval [63.16%, 82.76%]. EERIE classified as ordinary (normal) difficulty.

objectives: Classify words into three difficulty levels.
constraints: Standard assumptions of the method apply.

parameter_estimation.method: Cross-validation for K selection. Best K=8, accuracy 75.28%.

steps: Select K=8 via cross-validation on accuracy.
Classify test word by majority vote of K nearest neighbors.

assumptions: Difficulty is determined by word features.
Median try count is a valid difficulty proxy.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: K=8 selected by CV; accuracy interval [63.16%, 82.76%].

validation_refs: Figure 12-13 covariance matrix and CV results.
limitations: Merging median-6 with median-5 may lose granularity.
